name: Rear Shocks & Springs
description: Factory rear uses a separate coil spring seated in the lower control arm pocket and a shock mounted from the LCA to the body shock pad (3 nuts). ZL1 = MRC monotube; ZL1 1LE = Multimatic DSSV (hard-mounted, auto vs manual specific tune). Race option: keep the split spring/shock layout with race shocks and springs, or convert to rear coilovers with coilover-specific LCAs.

components.name: Rear shock absorber / damper
components.description: Rear damper from the outboard end of the lower control arm up to the body shock pad. On the factory layout the LCA motion ratio at the shock is below 1, so damping must be valved for that ratio. The lower bolt is a torque-angle single-use bolt.
components.location: Lower mount on LCA approx (x 2.84, y 0.21, z +/-0.62) to upper mount approx (x 2.75, y 0.70, z +/-0.58).

factory.name: ZL1: MRC monotube; ZL1 1LE: Multimatic DSSV (hard mounted)
factory.notes: 1LE rear tune differs between manual and 10-speed automatic cars (GM bulletin 19-NA-038). SG3 kit 84408106 includes non-MRC rear shocks + new lower bolts.

raceOptions.name: Double/triple-adjustable race shocks (Penske, JRi, MCS, Öhlins)
raceOptions.notes: Build to factory eye-to-eye and mounting, or as coilovers with BMR LCA361/LCA362.

raceOptions.name: KW V3 / Clubsport rear dampers
raceOptions.notes: Verify Gen 6 fitment/type (split spring vs coilover rear).

hardware.item: Rear shock absorber lower bolt (shock to LCA)
hardware.spec: Flange bolt + nut (15/18 mm per BMR); GM P/N 11609598 per BMR list
hardware.torqueSequence: First pass 100 N·m (74 lb ft), final pass +90-105 deg
hardware.notes: BMR cradle-bushing instructions quote 83 ft-lb straight torque; use the GM torque-angle value with a new bolt.

hardware.item: Rear shock upper mount nuts (to body)

installNotes: Remove rear wheelhouse liner (retainers, screws, 2 fascia bolts) for access to the upper nuts.
Support LCA with a jack; remove lower bolt (discard), then the 3 upper nuts.
Install new shock: upper nuts 43 N·m, new lower bolt 100 N·m + 90-105 deg.
inspection: Check for leaks and top mount condition; record clicker settings.

components.name: Rear coil spring (on lower control arm)
components.description: Separate rear coil spring between the LCA spring pocket and a body spring seat, inboard of the shock. Because it sits partway along the LCA, its motion ratio is well below 1 - wheel rate is approx spring rate x MR^2, so rear springs are much stiffer than the wheel rate they produce. Spring tag goes at the top (toward upper insulator).

factory.name: GM rear coil spring (rate by RPO)

raceOptions.name: Race rear spring for factory pocket (Eibach, Hyperco - custom)
raceOptions.notes: Barrel/pigtail ends must match the pocket and insulators.

installNotes: Compress spring by raising LCA with a jack; never let the LCA drop with spring loaded (GM warning).
Ensure spring is seated in both insulators with insulator stops against the last coil.

components.name: Rear coilover conversion (race option)
components.description: Moves the rear spring onto the damper (coilover) at the shock location, removing the factory spring pocket load. Gives threaded-perch ride height/corner-weight adjustment and lets spring rates be changed quickly. Requires coilover-specific LCAs (e.g. BMR LCA361/LCA362) and reinforcement of the rear shock pads since they now carry full spring load.

raceOptions.name: BMR LCA361 / LCA362 coilover lower control arms
raceOptions.notes: Note camber bolt position before removal; reuse factory shock, camber and spindle hardware.
